high.title: Kuo Ming-chien Resigns as Cathay United Bank Chairman; Cathay Financial to Appoint Him as Senior Advisor
high.summary:
Kuo Ming-chien has resigned from his positions as Director of Cathay Financial Holdings, Chairman and Director of Cathay United Bank, and Director of Cathay Private Equity, citing public controversy over his concurrent outside roles. The resignation follows a related-party transaction scandal at Cathay Securities Investment Trust (Cathay SITE), where Kuo simultaneously served on the board of Cathay SITE and as an independent director of Alchip Technologies (世芯-KY), rendering Alchip a related-party company. Despite this conflict, Cathay SITE's discretionary accounts and eight fund portfolios continued to trade Alchip shares — triggering mandatory NAV recalculations and investor compensation obligations.

Total compensation to be paid is approximately NT$490 million, covering roughly 50,500 beneficiaries across 47 distribution institutions. Cathay SITE states it is applying a "most favorable" compensation principle. Cathay Financial has also initiated a broader audit of all domestic and foreign companies where Kuo concurrently served as director or independent director during his tenure.

**Market Implications:** This is a significant governance incident for Cathay Financial Holdings (2882.TW), Taiwan's largest financial conglomerate. The NT$490M compensation liability, while manageable, raises concerns about internal compliance controls at Cathay SITE. Investors should monitor potential FSC regulatory action, reputational risk to the Cathay brand, and any further revelations from the ongoing audit of Kuo's other concurrent directorships. The episode may prompt broader regulatory scrutiny of related-party investment practices across Taiwan's asset management industry.

high.title: Surprise: Qualcomm's AI Transformation Names UMC as Winner — TSMC's Absence Sparks Debate
high.summary:
At its annual investor day on June 24, Qualcomm unveiled its largest-ever strategic transformation, targeting the AI data center market and announcing 35 ecosystem partners. In the foundry segment, United Microelectronics Corporation (UMC, 2303.TW) was the sole wafer foundry listed — with TSMC conspicuously absent — generating significant industry discussion. Industry analysts interpret the partnership as extending beyond conventional foundry services to encompass advanced packaging-integrated power delivery technologies critical for high-power AI chips. Specifically, the collaboration is believed to focus on FinFET power management ICs, on-wafer inductors, and deep trench capacitors (DTC) — areas where UMC holds deep expertise in mature and specialty process nodes.

UMC CEO Jason Wang was directly quoted in Qualcomm's press release, stating that advanced packaging and manufacturing collaboration is increasingly vital for next-generation data center performance, energy efficiency, and scalability. Qualcomm also unveiled its "Dragonfly" product family, including the Dragonfly C1000 data center CPU and AI300 series.

**Market Implications:** This development is a meaningful positive re-rating catalyst for UMC (2303.TW), which has faced narrative headwinds as a "mature node" foundry in an era dominated by leading-edge process competition. Selection as Qualcomm's sole foundry partner for its AI data center push signals that UMC's specialty process and packaging integration capabilities are commercially differentiated. For TSMC (2330.TW), the omission warrants monitoring — though it may reflect strategic or customer diversification decisions by Qualcomm rather than competitive displacement. Fund managers with positions in UMC should reassess the stock's AI supply chain exposure and potential upside revision to order forecasts.

high.title: [OpenAI's First Custom AI Chip "Jalapeño" Design Completed — Taiwan Supply Chain Set to Benefit]
high.summary:
OpenAI has announced the completion of its first custom-designed AI chip, "Jalapeño," developed in partnership with Broadcom. Critically for Taiwan equity investors, the chip is manufactured by **TSMC (2330)**, with industry sources confirming that volume production ramp-up is expected to progressively expand TSMC's advanced process node order book. The chip is designed for AI inference workloads — delivering AI services to enterprise and consumer users — while large-scale model training continues to rely on other chip architectures.

OpenAI's ultimate ambition is to deploy sufficient proprietary silicon to power 10GW of computing capacity globally. Beyond TSMC, the article highlights that **Hon Hai (鴻海)** and **Quanta (廣達)** stand to benefit as OpenAI scales into ASIC server applications, with both companies positioned as potential AI server manufacturing partners.

The nine-month design-to-completion timeline signals accelerating AI infrastructure buildout. For fund managers, this reinforces the structural demand thesis for TSMC's advanced nodes (3nm/2nm), while also flagging incremental revenue upside for Hon Hai in AI server assembly. Investors should monitor TSMC's forward order commentary and any Hon Hai supply chain confirmations at upcoming investor days.

---

high.title: Foreign Investors Sell NT$250 Billion in Taiwan Stocks Over Three Days; Analysts Expect Post-Quarter Rebalancing Before Index Targets 50,000
high.summary:
Foreign investors continued their aggressive selling streak in Taiwan equities, offloading a cumulative NT$256.5 billion over three consecutive sessions — the single largest three-day net sell figure in recent memory. The prior session alone saw foreign investors dump NT$177.4 billion, a historic single-day record. While yesterday's net sell figure moderated significantly to NT$40.51 billion, Taiwan futures net short positions remained at 81,051 contracts — still the second-highest level on record — signaling sustained caution from offshore institutions.

The TAIEX stabilized, closing up 211 points (+0.4%) at 46,255, aided by strong Micron earnings that eased AI demand concerns and active support from government-linked "national team" funds (eight major state banks collectively bought NT$70.8 billion over three days). Domestic investment trusts also continued net buying for a third straight session at NT$17.41 billion.

Market implications are significant: the scale of foreign selling suggests quarter-end portfolio rebalancing rather than a fundamental reassessment, but elevated futures short positions and high domestic leverage create conditions for continued near-term volatility. Institutional consensus anticipates a resumption of upward momentum toward the 50,000-point target once seasonal rebalancing concludes. Fund managers should monitor whether foreign net selling continues to decelerate and watch for any reduction in futures short positions as a key technical signal.

---

high.title: [Taiwan Stock Market Drops Over 1,000 Points — IC Design Sector Hit Hardest; MediaTek Hits Limit-Down, Realtek and Novatek Plunge in Tandem]
high.summary:
Taiwan's equity market saw intraday losses exceed 1,000 points on June 26, with IC design stocks bearing the brunt of the selloff. MediaTek (2454) hit its daily limit-down at NT$3,880, while Realtek (2379) fell 7.37% to NT$754 and Novatek (3034) dropped 8.38% to NT$514. Market participants note the decline is not driven by company-specific fundamental deterioration, but rather reflects profit-taking and deleveraging following significant run-ups tied to AI ASIC, edge AI, Wi-Fi 7, product price hike narratives, and consumer electronics recovery themes. UBS remains constructive on MediaTek, citing product price increases, the Google TPU project, smartphone SoC demand, and emerging applications; UBS raised its target price to NT$6,500 and anticipates accelerating growth from Q4 onwards. However, UBS also flagged that MediaTek may implement broad-based price hikes of 5–10% from September due to rising costs in advanced process nodes, back-end packaging, and substrate materials. Realtek highlighted that AI networking, Wi-Fi 7, automotive Ethernet, and high-speed switch demand remain H2 growth drivers, though router/broadband equipment adoption is slower than expected due to elevated memory costs. **Market implication:** The sharp reversal in high-beta IC design names signals a near-term risk-off rotation; fund managers should assess whether this is a healthy consolidation within an intact uptrend or the beginning of a broader derating of Taiwan's AI-adjacent semiconductor sub-sector.

---

high.title: Taiwan Stock Market Plunges Over 1,500 Points Intraday, Breaking Below 45,000; Eight Major Electronic Blue-Chips Hammered, Only ASE Holds Green
high.summary:
Taiwan's equity market suffered a severe intraday selloff on June 26, with the TAIEX plunging as much as 1,587 points to a low of 44,667 — breaching the psychologically critical 45,000 level and falling below the monthly moving average. The session opened at 46,188, but selling pressure intensified rapidly across the board.

**TSMC (2330)** led the damage, opening at NT$2,360 and sliding to NT$2,340 intraday, dragging the index by over 350 points on its own. Its ADR had already declined 1.32% overnight despite the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index surging 3.59%, driven by Micron's blowout earnings (+15.74%). Apple's sharp 6%+ decline appears to have weighed heavily on sentiment toward the broader tech supply chain.

**MediaTek (2454)** was another major casualty, hitting limit-down at NT$3,880 — a drop below the NT$4,000 threshold — contributing approximately 190 index points of downside pressure, though over 1,000 lots of buy orders were queued at the limit-down price. **Hon Hai (2317)** saw a more contained decline of ~2.5%, with the NT$250 level offering support. **Delta Electronics (2308)** fell over 8%, reaching NT$1,815. **ASE Technology (3711)** was the sole major electronic blue-chip holding gains.

**Market Implications:** The severity of this correction — driven by divergent U.S. overnight signals and outsized TSMC ADR weakness — suggests institutional and foreign investor de-risking. Fund managers should monitor whether the monthly moving average holds on a closing basis, and watch for foreign investor net buy/sell data as a key sentiment indicator.

high.title: Evergreen Marine Responds: Crew, Vessel, and Cargo Safe — Ship Has Safely Transited the Strait of Hormuz
high.summary:
Evergreen Marine (2603) confirmed that its Singapore-flagged vessel *Ever Lovely* was struck by an unidentified projectile near the Omani coast while transiting the Strait of Hormuz on June 25 at 21:55 Taipei time. The impact damaged the eave area and bridge windows on the starboard side of the superstructure. Following initial crew inspection, Evergreen confirmed that personnel, vessel, and cargo are all safe, with main engines and navigation systems fully operational and no seaworthiness issues. The vessel has since safely exited the strait. Two additional vessels — *Ever Unicorn* and *Ever Lotus* — have also cleared the Hormuz Strait without incident. Evergreen states no vessels remain trapped within the Persian Gulf.

**Market Implications:** While the immediate operational risk appears contained, the incident highlights ongoing geopolitical vulnerabilities in Persian Gulf shipping lanes. For investors in Evergreen Marine and broader shipping sector names, this warrants monitoring of future route decisions, war-risk insurance premiums, and any regulatory guidance on Hormuz transits. Escalation risk in the region could affect freight rates and operating costs for Taiwan's shipping companies.

high.title: Foreign Investors Aggressively Selling TSMC; Stock Breaks Below Monthly Moving Average, Testing NT$2,300 Level Ahead of July Investor Conference
high.summary: Foreign investors have been aggressively offloading TSMC (2330) shares, recording net selling for three consecutive trading days through June 25. Yesterday alone, foreign investors sold a net NT$40.51 billion across the centralized market, with TSMC topping the sell list. Cumulative foreign net selling in TSMC over the three-day period reached 47,280 thousand shares (張), dragging the stock below its monthly moving average. Intraday, TSMC touched a low of NT$2,325 — briefly falling below its ticker number of 2330 — before stabilizing in a narrow range around NT$2,335. Market capitalization declined to approximately NT$60.55 trillion. Foreign futures net short positions remain elevated at 81,051 contracts, though marginally reduced by 2,554 contracts. All eyes are now on TSMC's July investor conference for updated guidance. **Market Implication:** Sustained foreign selling pressure on TSMC is a major headwind for the broader TAIEX given TSMC's outsized index weighting. A confirmed break below the monthly moving average could trigger further technical selling. The July earnings call will be a critical catalyst — any downward revision to outlook could intensify the correction.

high.title: Taiwan Stock Market Plunges Over 1,000 Points Intraday; TSMC and Major Tech Weights Drag Index Below Key Levels — ASE Leads OSAT Stocks in Counter-Trend Resistance
high.summary: Taiwan's TAIEX suffered a sharp intraday decline of over 1,000 points on June 26, touching a low of 45,249 points, before partially recovering to around 45,471 points (down ~783 points) as of the time of reporting. The selloff was driven by three converging factors: (1) U.S. May PCE inflation data came in at 4.1% YoY (core PCE +3.4% YoY), reigniting market expectations for further Federal Reserve rate hikes; (2) weakness in large-cap U.S. tech stocks, particularly Apple (-6.1% on product price increases due to rising memory/storage costs), Nvidia, Microsoft, and Alphabet; and (3) TSMC's ADR declining 1.32% overnight, sending Taiwan index futures down 722 points in the night session to 45,805. Foreign futures net short positions remain above 80,000 contracts. Bucking the downtrend, OSAT (outsourced semiconductor assembly and test) stocks emerged as a defensive pocket, with ASE Technology (3711) surging over 5% intraday to NT$674. **Market Implication:** The dual pressure of Fed rate hike fears and foreign institutional selling represents a significant risk-off environment. The PCE print above 4% suggests inflation stickiness that may delay any Fed pivot, with direct implications for Taiwan's rate-sensitive sectors including life insurers and financial stocks. OSAT rotation warrants monitoring as a potential sector rotation signal.

high.title: Wistron Board Approves USD 150M Capital Injection into California Subsidiary After Nvidia's Jensen Huang Praises US Factory Expansion
high.summary:
Wistron (3231.TW) held a board meeting on June 26 and approved two major resolutions tied to aggressive global capacity expansion. The headline item is a USD 150 million capital injection into its wholly-owned California subsidiary, WisLab EMS Corporation, to support US operations expansion. Additionally, the board greenlit new capex across multiple geographies: TWD 1.7 billion for its Hsinchu facility, TWD 7.5 billion for Kaohsiung, USD 24.5 million for Vietnam, and USD 22.7 million for Malaysia.

The timing is highly strategic — just one day prior, Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang explicitly named Wistron among key supply chain partners building out US manufacturing capacity to underpin the AI ecosystem, during Nvidia's annual shareholder meeting. Huang highlighted the transition from generative AI toward "AI Agent" capabilities, repositioning AI data centers as continuous value-generating "AI factories."

high.title: Taiwan Stock Market Plunges 1,683 Points for Fourth Consecutive Down Day — MediaTek Hits Limit Down, TSMC Falls NT$50
high.summary: Taiwan's equity market suffered a severe sell-off on June 26, closing down 1,683.5 points (-3.64%) at 44,571.76, marking the fourth consecutive down session. TSMC (2330) closed at NT$2,340, falling NT$50 (-2.09%), while MediaTek (2454) hit its daily limit-down, breaching the critical NT$4,000 level. Delta Electronics (2308) dropped approximately 9%. The three stocks combined accounted for 815 index points of the decline. Turnover was exceptionally heavy at NT$1.5498 trillion. The trigger was a combination of persistent concerns over U.S. rate hike risks and elevated tech valuations, compounded by sharp falls in Japanese and Korean equities in early Asian trading. First Capital Investment Advisory cited the surge in U.S. May PCE inflation to 4.1% as a key driver of investor anxiety over Fed policy direction. All short- and medium-term moving average supports have been breached. **Market Implication:** The breakdown of key technical levels and the magnitude of losses in large-cap tech names signal significant near-term downside risk for Taiwan equities. Portfolio managers should reassess exposure to high-beta technology names and monitor Fed policy signals closely.

high.title: Three Institutional Investors Net Sell NT$205.5 Billion — Foreign Investors Post Second-Largest Single-Day Sell-Off in History; Taiwan Market Records Third-Largest Point Drop Ever
high.summary: Taiwan's three major institutional investors collectively net sold NT$205.527 billion on June 26, an extraordinary single-session outflow. Foreign and mainland Chinese investors (excluding foreign proprietary desks) net sold NT$143.189 billion — the second-largest foreign sell-off on record — while this week's cumulative foreign selling has already set both the all-time single-week record for the largest and second-largest daily sell-overs. Proprietary dealers also sold heavily at a net NT$70.733 billion (combined), while investment trusts bucked the trend with a modest net purchase of NT$8.395 billion. The TAIEX recorded its third-largest point decline in history on a closing basis at -1,683.5 points, with 1,819 declining stocks versus only 165 advancing, and 37 stocks hitting limit-down. Intraday the index fell as deep as 1,801 points to 44,454.22, breaching the 45,000 psychological level before a late-session partial recovery. **Market Implication:** The scale and speed of foreign institutional selling is exceptional and warrants close monitoring. The consecutive record-breaking foreign outflows suggest a possible structural re-rating event rather than a short-term correction. Fund managers should assess currency hedging positions and monitor for potential NT dollar depreciation pressure stemming from sustained foreign equity outflows.

medium.title: U.S. Market Close: Apple Price Hikes Weigh on Sentiment; Micron Drives Semiconductor Rally but Fails to Save Nasdaq — Fourth Consecutive Day of Losses
medium.summary:
U.S. equities closed mixed on Thursday. Micron Technology delivered blowout quarterly results — with revenues quadrupling year-over-year and a far-above-consensus forward outlook — driving the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index up 3.6%, on track for its strongest quarter on record. However, Apple's announcement of price increases on Mac and iPad products undermined broader tech and consumer sentiment, contributing to the Nasdaq's fourth consecutive daily decline, its longest losing streak since March. The Dow Jones gained 0.1% to 51,920, the S&P 500 was essentially flat at 7,357, and the Nasdaq fell 0.5% to 25,358. TSMC ADRs declined 1.3%. Notably, May PCE inflation rose to 4.1% year-over-year — the first breach of the 4% threshold in three years — driven by elevated energy costs and AI infrastructure investment, though core PCE monthly gain of 0.3% met expectations.

**Relevance to Taiwan:** TSMC ADR weakness and the semiconductor index's strength present a mixed signal for Taiwan's chip sector. The PCE inflation data reinforces a cautious Fed outlook, which may sustain USD strength and pressure the New Taiwan Dollar — a key variable for Taiwan life insurers' overseas investment returns and hedging costs.

medium.title: Evergreen Marine's "Ever Lovely" Vessel Attacked; IMO Suspends Hormuz Strait Evacuation Plan — New Variable for U.S.-Iran Ceasefire
medium.summary:
The IMO announced the suspension of its assisted evacuation plan for vessels stranded in the Strait of Hormuz after a ship transiting the waterway was attacked Thursday, with a U.S. official attributing the strike to Iranian military forces. The attacked vessel has been identified by two sources as the "Ever Lovely," a Singapore-flagged containership operated by Evergreen Marine (2603.TW), with a capacity of 8,508 TEUs. No casualties were reported. The incident introduces fresh uncertainty into the temporary U.S.-Iran agreement signed last week aimed at reopening the strait and extending the ceasefire by 60 days. Evergreen Marine did not immediately respond to requests for comment.

**Market Implications:** This is a material near-term risk for Evergreen Marine (2603.TW) and Taiwan's broader shipping sector. A prolonged Hormuz closure or escalating geopolitical instability would disrupt global container routing, potentially affecting freight rates and fleet deployment. Investors in Evergreen and Yang Ming (2609.TW) should monitor developments closely. Insurance exposure and vessel damage assessments are pending.

medium.title: [Micron's Blowout Results and Outlook Lift Taiwan PCB Suppliers Unimicron and Health-Way]
medium.summary: Memory giant Micron delivered a market-beating quarterly report and issued guidance indicating no visible timeline for supply catching up with demand, reinforcing a sustained memory upcycle. Institutional investors expect continued positive spillover to Taiwan's memory-adjacent supply chain, including **Unimicron (健鼎)** and **Taiwan Surface Mounting Technology (台表科, 6278)**. Unimicron reported May consolidated revenue of NT$8.654 billion — a second consecutive monthly record — up 5.5% MoM and 46.6% YoY, with cumulative January–May revenue growing 28.7% YoY. Taiwan SMT, a key DDR5/DRAM module SMT/PCBA supplier, maintains a positive H2 outlook and plans to add ten production lines in 2026, targeting 5–10% full-year revenue growth. The Micron read-through also benefits South Asia Technology (南亞科) and Winbond (華邦). This article is relevant as a secondary indicator of AI and server infrastructure demand feeding into Taiwan's broader technology hardware supply chain.

medium.title: [Jensen Huang: Physical AI Is NVIDIA's Next Growth Wave]
medium.summary: At NVIDIA's annual shareholder meeting, CEO Jensen Huang declared the company has entered a new era of AI infrastructure, describing the current phase as a "pivotal growth stage." Huang confirmed that AI infrastructure has graduated from experimentation to full-scale production, a cycle he expects to persist for decades. He identified **physical AI** — encompassing robotics, autonomous vehicles, and smart factories — as NVIDIA's next major growth vector, with a complete ecosystem already built via AI factories, Omniverse digital twins, Jetson edge computing, and the Cosmos world foundation model. Huang also addressed export control compliance, warning that smuggled chips would receive no NVIDIA support or maintenance, effectively limiting illicit use in sanctioned markets. For Taiwan investors, this reinforces sustained demand for TSMC's leading-edge nodes and server supply chain companies including Hon Hai, given NVIDIA's continued infrastructure expansion ambitions.

medium.title: [AI Demand Drives North America Air Cargo Rates Higher Again in July]
medium.summary: Taiwan-to-North America air freight rates are set to rise again in July, increasing from approximately NT$300/kg to NT$320–350/kg, driven primarily by surging AI-related cargo demand despite falling fuel surcharges — an unusual divergence highlighting the structural strength of AI hardware shipments. Industry analysis confirms that AI logistics has become an embedded supply chain in Taiwan, benefiting listed carriers **China Airlines (華航, 2610)**, EVA Air, and Starlux, as well as logistics operators including 中菲行, 捷迅, 台驊, and 台灣空運. **Farglory Port's** air free trade zone has emerged as an AI chip industry cluster and is expected to achieve record operating performance this year. The logistics industry outlook for H2 and Q4 remains bullish, underpinned by continued hyperscaler capex from Microsoft, Google, Meta, and Amazon. This is relevant for fund managers with exposure to Taiwan's aviation and logistics sectors as a proxy for AI hardware export momentum.

medium.title: Evergreen Shipping Vessel "Ever Lovely" Struck by Drone in Strait of Hormuz; U.S.-Iran Peace Deal Under Pressure
medium.summary: Iran's Revolutionary Guard attacked the Singapore-flagged cargo vessel "Ever Lovely," owned by Evergreen Marine Asia (a subsidiary of Taiwan-listed Evergreen Marine), in the Strait of Hormuz on June 25 using a one-way attack drone, causing damage to the ship's bridge but no casualties. The IMO subsequently suspended escort operations through the strait. The incident directly tests the preliminary U.S.-Iran peace agreement signed the previous week and raises renewed concerns about Persian Gulf shipping security. For Taiwan-listed shipping investors, this is a material near-term risk event for Evergreen Marine Corp (2603) and related logistics names. Prolonged disruption to Hormuz transit routes could impact freight rates and operational costs, though the vessel had already been stranded in the Persian Gulf for over 100 days prior to the attack.

medium.title: [Taiwan Stock Market Expected to Surge Tomorrow — Three Key Catalysts]
medium.summary: Investment strategist Kuo Che-jung of Moore Investment Advisory notes that Taiwan's benchmark index rose 211 points (+0.46%) on June 25, lagging significantly behind Korea's 5%+ surge and Japan's near-record rally — a divergence he views as creating strong catch-up potential. He identifies three bullish catalysts for the following session: (1) significant underperformance relative to regional peers leaving room for catch-up buying; (2) resolution of the short-term chip overhang caused by Korean regulatory action on leveraged ETFs, which he views as a healthy de-froth of excess speculation; and (3) Micron's blowout quarterly earnings — with HBM capacity sold out through 2027 — which had not yet been fully priced into most Taiwan memory-related names beyond Nanya Tech. **Note for fund managers:** This article was published the evening of June 25, and the subsequent June 26 article above confirms the market did not in fact surge as predicted, underscoring the importance of scrutinizing directional calls from sell-side commentators.

medium.title: [Taiwan Stock Market Arena — Analyst Chuang Chia-ying: H2 Seasonality + AI Application Deployment Supports Medium-to-Long-Term Bullish Bias]
medium.summary: Analyst Chuang Chia-ying offers a constructive medium-term outlook for Taiwan equities, citing H2 seasonal demand tailwinds and increasing real-world AI application deployment. She notes that on June 25 Taiwan's index closed up 211 points at 46,255, supported by Micron's strong earnings beat driven by HBM and AI server demand — with management guiding for continued memory market tightness beyond 2027. Taiwan's May export orders came in at USD 89.48 billion, up 47.2% YoY, marking the 16th consecutive month of positive year-over-year growth and the second-highest single-month figure on record, with June expected to show further expansion. U.S. markets were mixed, with the Dow edging higher while Nasdaq and the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index pulled back amid concerns over elevated AI sector valuations, rising big-tech capex, and the prospect of a prolonged Fed hold on rates. This macro backdrop — strong Taiwan export fundamentals tempered by U.S. rate uncertainty — is a key framework for positioning in Taiwan listed technology names.

medium.title: [Ying Pai (Liqtech/Liqan — AI Chassis Maker) Secures Large Orders from NVIDIA and AMD; Set to Deliver Strong H2 2026 Results]
medium.summary: Ying Pai Enterprise (3693), a Taiwan-listed AI server chassis manufacturer, held its AGM on June 25 and expressed strong confidence in H2 2026 performance, buoyed by surging orders from both NVIDIA and AMD for their next-generation AI platforms. The company was notably spotlighted by NVIDIA CEO Jensen Huang at CES earlier this year as the sole newly added Taiwan supplier on NVIDIA's chassis reference board, deepening collaboration in AI storage infrastructure. On the AMD side, Ying Pai has begun work on rack-scale AI infrastructure projects utilizing AMD's next-generation platform, and is preparing to mass-produce cabinets and chassis featuring AMD's MI450 chips — with large-scale shipments expected in H2. AMD's MI400 series has already secured orders from OpenAI, Meta, and Anthropic. This positions Ying Pai as a meaningful beneficiary of the broader AI infrastructure buildout, with AI-segment revenue expected to grow as a share of total sales in FY2026.

medium.title: Shin Kong Mitsukoshi Announces Tainan Zhongshan Store to Close in October; Site Rumored for Major Redevelopment
medium.summary:
Shin Kong Mitsukoshi officially announced the closure of its Tainan Zhongshan store — open for nearly 30 years since 1996 — effective end of October 2026, following the expiration of its lease agreement. The company stated that Tainan New Sky City and the newly opened Tainan Xiaobei Men store will absorb the local customer base. Market sources indicate the original site is slated for a major redevelopment: lower floors are planned to become an open-concept lifestyle retail complex (potentially operated by the Taomall shopping center team), while upper floors (9F–13F) may be converted into an international chain hotel. This reflects broader structural pressures on traditional department store formats in Taiwan and the ongoing pivot toward mixed-use, experiential retail developments.

---

medium.title: Taiwan Stock Market Opens Sharply Lower — TSMC Breaks Monthly Moving Average; MediaTek, Hon Hai, Delta Among Key Weights Falling; ASE and PCB Stocks Show Resilience
medium.summary: Taiwan's stock market opened down 66.66 points on June 26 before rapidly accelerating losses to nearly 740 points as major tech bellwethers collapsed simultaneously. TSMC (2330) broke below its monthly moving average, dragging MediaTek (2454), Delta Electronics (2308), UMC (2303), and Hon Hai (2317) lower. The index breached the 46,000-point level and fell below its 10-day moving average. On the positive side, ASE Investment Holdings (3711) and PCB/substrate names including Nan Ya PCB (8046), Jing Sheng (3189), Unimicron (3037), and Zhen Ding-KY (4958) showed relative strength. The overnight catalyst was mixed U.S. markets, where the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index rose 3.59% on Micron's strong earnings (stock +15.74%), but Apple's 6%+ decline weighed on Nasdaq for its fourth consecutive losing session. This article provides useful early-session context that anticipated the more severe intraday drop detailed in subsequent reporting.

medium.title: MediaTek (2454) Breaks Below NT$4,000 Psychological Level Amid Broad Market Correction
medium.summary: MediaTek (2454) broke below the key NT$4,000 psychological support level in morning trading on June 26, despite a constructive medium-term fundamental outlook. The company had previously guided Q2 revenue (at USD/TWD of 31.5) in the range of NT$140.2–149.2 billion, representing a QoQ decline of 6% to flat and YoY decline of 7% to -1%. Cumulative January–May revenue reached NT$243.32 billion (-1.5% YoY). On a positive note, MediaTek is advancing on multiple growth fronts: its CPU co-developed with Nvidia for the RTX Spark AI PC chip, AI ASIC development for U.S. hyperscalers (on track for mass production), and an anticipated ~US$2 billion revenue contribution from AI ASIC in Q4 2025. Full-year USD revenue is expected to grow mid-to-high single digits (~4–9% YoY). The NT$4,000 breach is technically significant and may trigger additional stop-loss selling in the near term, though the AI ASIC pipeline provides a medium-term fundamental anchor.

medium.title: U.S. May PCE In Line with Expectations; Taiwan Index Futures Night Session Reverses from Losses to Gains
medium.summary: U.S. May core PCE came in at +3.4% YoY, in line with market expectations. Taiwan index futures (night session, June 25) initially opened lower at 46,430 before recovering to 46,740 (up 213 points, +0.4%), touching a high of 46,884. Analysts at Yong Feng Futures noted that while Micron's better-than-expected earnings redirected market focus toward AI and memory recovery themes, a single positive catalyst is unlikely to confirm the end of the corrective phase given the TAIEX's large prior run-up and continued overhead supply pressure from foreign and short-term investors. Key technical focus is on the monthly moving average — a sustained consolidation near that level with declining volume would be constructive, while a failure to hold would suggest the correction is ongoing. Note: This article's PCE figure of 3.4% for core (vs. 4.1% headline cited in Article 4) is consistent with consensus; the divergence in the two articles' PCE headline figures warrants monitoring for data clarification.

medium.title: SCFI Freight Rate Index Rises for Ninth Consecutive Week; US West Coast Rates Surge 11% — Taiwan Container Shipping Trio Poised for Strong Q3
medium.summary: The Shanghai Containerized Freight Index (SCFI) extended its winning streak to nine consecutive weeks, reaching 3,239.64 points — up 3.8% week-on-week — as all four major shipping lanes continued to strengthen. Far East to US West Coast rates climbed 11.4% to USD 6,067/FEU, while Far East to US East Coast rates rose 8.9% to USD 7,484/FEU. European routes also advanced, with Far East to Europe up to USD 3,342/TEU. Carriers are planning further General Rate Increases (GRI) of approximately USD 1,500 effective July 1, with the US Northwest and East Coast routes seen as most likely to absorb the full increase.

medium.title: Taiwan Market Breaks Monthly Moving Average, but ABF Substrate Leaders Hold Relatively Firm — Nanya PCB Surges to All-Time High
medium.summary: Despite the broader market plunging over 1,000 points intraday and breaching its monthly moving average, ABF substrate stocks demonstrated relative resilience. Nanya PCB (8046) briefly locked at its limit-up price of NT$1,145, setting a new all-time high before the limit broke, ending up approximately 7%. Ching Song (3189) fell only marginally, while Unimicron (3037) and Zhen Ding (4958) declined 2–3%. Foreign analysts project the ABF substrate supply-demand deficit will widen from approximately 4% in 2026 to 10% in 2027 and 16% in 2028, supporting continued price increases — with high single-digit price hikes already recorded in Q2 2026 and double-digit increases expected in Q3. The broadening of demand beyond AI servers into general-purpose servers driven by agentic AI architectures is cited as an incremental positive. Meanwhile, TSMC (2330) fell nearly 2% and also broke its monthly moving average, and Hon Hai (2317) declined over 3%. **Implication:** ABF substrate companies represent a potential defensive sector within the broader tech sell-off, supported by multi-year structural supply constraints.

medium.title: Micron Surges 16% on Earnings Beat, But Memory Stocks Reverse as Asian Markets Collapse
medium.summary: Micron reported strong quarterly results — both last quarter's performance and current-quarter guidance exceeded consensus expectations — and management indicated AI-driven memory supply shortages are expected to persist beyond 2027, with 16 long-term supply agreements signed with customers. Micron shares surged 15.7%, lifting SanDisk (+21.97%), Qualcomm (+3.8%), and the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index (+3.6%). However, the positive memory narrative was overwhelmed by broader risk-off sentiment: Apple fell over 6% after announcing price increases on MacBooks and iPads, Microsoft dropped 3.5% after raising Xbox prices, and the Nasdaq closed lower for a fourth consecutive session. In Taiwan, memory-related stocks initially opened higher but reversed to the downside as the Korean KOSPI briefly triggered a circuit breaker (falling over 8%) and the Nikkei declined over 4.5%. Macro Electronics (2337) was a notable exception, holding in positive territory. **Implication:** Near-term memory sector sentiment remains hostage to macro risk-off dynamics despite strong fundamental catalysts; investors should monitor whether Micron's supply guidance translates to sustainable re-rating once volatility subsides.
